name: AOCI-CODE v0.2.0-rc2
body:
AOCI-CODE v0.2.0-rc2 is built from `51ca8c2286e7a3eff2fcedc22099951d43264494`.


The second 0.2.0 candidate: fixes and host-side findings from two weeks of
v0.2.0-rc1 in use, with no new subsystem. Three of the fixes close loops that
cost a Host rounds without end: an Entry for a file named `#...` that was
written but never read back, a repeated orphan removal that wedged or was
refused, and handed-back commands that only ran from the repository root.
A repository governed by v0.2.0-rc1 needs no migration. One recovery receipt
changed shape: finish an in-flight `aoci_remove_entry` with this binary before
going back to an older one.

Changes:

- An orphan that was removed, recreated, and removed again no longer wedges
  the repository. `aoci_remove_entry` used the object's own hash as the Ledger
  transaction identity, so the second removal wrote its Volume and Baseline,
  then conflicted with the first removal's Ledger event and left a pending
  receipt that no retry could close, blocking every other governance write
  (#176, present since 0.1.x; fix by yunshihang, #177). Each removal now
  records its own identity in a version-2 receipt; version-1 receipts stay
  readable, and an older binary must not be used to recover a version-2 one.
  The batch route had the same collision in another place: a batch of
  `removals` alone is identified by its paths, so the earlier removal's
  archived receipt answered the later one with a postimage conflict and no
  write, and Maintain kept listing the orphan. Such a batch now gets its own
  receipt and Ledger identity whenever one of its paths carries an Entry
  again. Scenario B6 walks both routes.
- A file whose name begins with `#` (`#hash.txt`, an editor's `#draft#`) is
  indexed like any other. Its Entry line begins with `#`, which every reader
  took for a comment while the writer accepted it: the write was reported
  applied, the Entry was never read back, and every Maintain round issued the
  same candidate again and appended one more copy to the Volume, for as long
  as the Host kept running rounds. Present since 0.1.x; reported by the
  aoci-agent project. Inside a directory section a `#` line is now a comment
  only when it lacks the Entry shape. A Volume already carrying those copies
  reads as aligned after the upgrade (the last copy is the Entry) and the next
  write removes the rest. A batch whose Entry would not read back from the
  Volume it publishes is refused before any write, naming the object.
- Built with Go 1.26.11, which fixes GO-2026-6859 (an HTTP/1 server crash in
  `net/http`). In AOCI only the loopback status page serves HTTP.
- A host dialog that comes back as `decline` is `status=dismissed`, not
  `rejected`: a Host that cannot show the dialog, or times it out, answers
  decline without the person seeing it, and that used to be recorded as the
  person's refusal. Only the form's own Reject choice is a rejection.
- `aoci check` concludes "governance aligned" instead of "ready to commit":
  it proves bookkeeping, not what the Entries say. The aligned line of verify,
  check, and status now adds how many index-role sources carry no Entry by
  rule and why, where "369 Entries cover 379 sources" read as ten uncovered.
- Docs: a `.mcp.json` example for Claude Code on Windows with the repository
  in WSL.
- Saving a Baseline whose content did not change leaves the file untouched,
  `updated_at` included. The timestamp was re-stamped on every save, so two
  branches holding the same managed set conflicted on that one line when
  merged and a scan that found nothing dirtied the tree (#173).
- `aoci init` under a custom `index_path` no longer writes a Legacy skeleton,
  a layout that has been read-only since 0.2.0 and whose only next step was to
  migrate an empty index. It refuses, writes nothing, and names the fix
  (`aoci config set index_path aoci.txt`).
- Harness: the upgrade axis retries transient release downloads (#169), and
  `ledger_timings.py` skips malformed Ledger rows and exits 0 on `--help`
  (#170, #171, dayebishouji). `internal/cognitionbaseline` has package tests
  and a real coverage floor; a reflection test keeps every Guide command field
  in the bound list.
- Overview delivery rules say what a Host must do about a truncated Chunk:
  request each Chunk in its own tool call, and when the Host truncates one,
  request the same cursor once more and check `chunk_sha256` before anything
  else. Lowering `overview_delivery.chunk_tokens` and restarting is left for a
  single Chunk that is truncated twice. The old rule sent every truncation
  there, which does not cure Chunks merged into one script output and walked
  one repository's team setting down to the 4000 floor (50 round trips per
  read). The attestation prompt now spells the four answer keys.
- Six host-side findings from the v0.2.0-rc1 adaptation (#168): a cognition
  optimization batch delivered again keeps the `explicit_object_ref` reason
  it was opened with; one `repair_required` now carries each candidate's
  field token budget overruns beside its form and length findings, as the
  tool description always said; every Maintain and Apply receipt names its
  Volumes with their paths in `delivered_volumes`, as Overview did; the Host
  capacity verdict is cleared by a later confirmed complete delivery of a
  scope that large, so a reload the Host itself stopped no longer keeps a
  long-lived server session source-bound; the delivery contract names the
  two cursor-failure tokens (`overview_snapshot_changed`,
  `overview_session_unavailable_restart_required`).
- `aoci scope rule add` accepts repeated `--pattern` flags before the first
  scan, for `--action exclude --pattern-kind directory` only: a project that
  defers several modules adds every exclusion in one validated edit instead of
  one command per directory. The rule ID argument prefixes a stable per-directory
  ID, the batch shares the first scan's lock, and an existing Baseline refuses
  it, so scanned repositories keep the Scope Change workflow. The Locale upgrade
  that rewrites team configuration now saves through CAS, so it cannot
  overwrite a concurrent policy edit. (dayebishouji, #167, refs #54)
- Every command AOCI hands a Host to run names its repository: `next_commands`
  from Maintain and Apply, the Guide's commands, onboarding's continuation,
  and the exact command an `interaction_required` answer prints all carry
  `--repo <root>` beside the absolute binary. A session that starts above or
  beside the repository, as a multi-repository Host session does, used to get
  commands that resolved the wrong tree, or none, when run from its own shell.
- Overview continuation checks every governed source through the fingerprint
  cache that scan and Maintain already trust, one stat per unchanged file
  instead of one read, and the Safe Inventory it rebuilds takes untracked
  paths from the status listing it already runs, one git process fewer on
  every governance call. Both matter most on Windows, where a 12-Chunk session
  start spent most of its server time rereading sources (#127, #150). A
  same-size rewrite that also restores the mtime is now unseen by the guard
  exactly as governance would miss it.
- The starter Meta names the neutral section root: one comment line says that
  `/<repository>` stands for the checkout holding the index, so a reader that
  has only the index file knows where `===/<repository>/docs/===` points.
- `aoci index relocate` gives an older index the same shape: it rewrites the
  recorded section roots to `/<repository>` and adds that Meta line, as one
  receipted transaction over Meta, Code Volume, and Baseline that running the
  command again resumes after a crash. This repository's own index now reads
  that way.
- `init --agent` on a clone no longer rewrites the committed Baseline for a
  host configuration Git ignores; init records only what scan would.
- `scope activate --reviewed-by <identity>` records the Observe review the
  activation would otherwise refuse on, over the paths the planner names, so a
  merge that changed both the rules and Observe files no longer waits on two
  commands that each wait for the other.
- Every governance call resolves the commit it binds from the files git keeps
  (a loose or packed ref, a detached HEAD, a linked worktree) and asks git only
  for a shape it does not understand: one process fewer per call.
- The capability manifest advertises `sqlite_schema_evidence` and lists
  Migration rollback and Bootstrap rollback among the terminal-only actions the
  interaction contract already reserved.
- `scripts/blackbox/ledger_timings.py` takes the index source count from any
  Ledger event that carries one, not only `check`.
- `docs/getting-started.md` says what a teammate does on a repository that
  already has an index, and `docs/mongodb-collection-evidence-profile.md`
  records the proposed MongoDB collection profile from #135 (#166).


See `docs/install.md` and `docs/supply-chain.md` for asset verification.

name: AOCI-CODE v0.2.0-rc1
body:
AOCI-CODE v0.2.0-rc1 is built from `91e3936ff65b77e8166ae83efdeacf2a7b00a193`.


The first 0.2.0 candidate: the speed work, the one-call closing, and
host-dialog approval, with the Legacy single-file write path retired. An entry
that changes a persisted preimage names the binary every machine then needs.

Upgrading from 0.1.x:

- A Legacy single-file index, an `aoci.txt` that carries its own Header and
  Entries, is read-only apart from a Managed Scope transaction;
  `aoci cognition onboard` migrates it.
- A tracked module named `logs` or `run` becomes a Missing Entry, because
  neither name is a built-in exclusion any more.
- The `aoci baseline scope` commands are gone; `aoci scope` covers them. A
  `baseline scope` transaction 0.1.x left pending is resumed with 0.1.x
  before the upgrade; this release reads its intent as an invalid scope
  receipt, which blocks the repository until it is moved out of
  `.aoci/transactions`.
- A repository initialized by this release uses `sensitive_name_rules` v2 and
  may declare a SQLite source. A 0.1.x binary answers such a repository with
  `scope_change_required` or refuses the declaration, so every machine that
  maintains it needs this release.

Changes:

- The Whole-Index maximum no longer refuses anything. An index may be read
  outside an Agent's context window, so its total size only names the budget
  status (`healthy`, `near_budget`, `warning`, `exceeded`): an Entry Apply, a
  Scope Change, `check`, the Guide, and `cognition_optimization` no longer
  stop when the Whole-Index passes `max_tokens`, and `scope status` no longer
  reports `cognition_compression_required`. In enforce mode the R and S limits
  still return an Entry over its limit to the model, and the Guide and
  `next_commands` for that stop now name the band
  (`scope budget set --policy-file {policy_file}`) instead of `--max-tokens`.
  No configuration or Baseline byte changes, so no repository needs a Scope
  Change; a 0.1.x binary still enforces the maximum on the same configuration.
- After a merge, a Code or Database Volume whose bytes no longer match the
  Baseline is restored together with the Root, every other Volume, and
  `.aoci/baseline.json` from one commit. The repair action of
  `code_volume_unbaselined` and `database_volume_unbaselined` used to say
  "restore them": restoring a Code Volume alone matched its own Baseline
  record while the Baseline still bound the other branch's sources, so an
  Entry that branch had re-authored went back to its older text and Maintain
  reported the repository aligned. Restored as one set, Maintain returns every
  source or table the restored Entries do not describe, after any Scope
  Change, Locale switch, or Observe review it names first. These two findings
  and `meta_volume_baseline_drift` no longer suggest re-establishing cognition
  through a Scope Change, because a Scope Change cannot rebaseline a formal
  Volume; `root_volume_baseline_drift` names it only for the Root an older
  Database Bootstrap left, the one Root drift a Scope Change reconciles.
  v0.1.x prints the old wording for every Volume; follow this one.
- Every batch of a `cognition_optimization` pass reports the floored S
  maximum. Since #146 only the batch that starts a pass carried an
  `s_max_tokens` floored by the Meta's S quota; the current batch delivered
  again and every later batch fell back to the machine default, under-reporting
  the limit Apply enforces wherever the Meta declares a looser quota. No
  identity or batch cut changes.
- `aoci config set locale` works on a Volumes v1 repository. It used to be
  refused once the index existed, so a repository created in one Locale
  could not move to the other without being rebuilt. The switch is one
  resumable transaction over the Root's `#Locale` line, the team
  configuration, and the Baseline record of the Root; the Meta, Code, and
  Database Volumes are guards and keep their bytes, so no Entry is rewritten.
  Locale is prospective: existing Entries keep their language, Entries
  created or updated afterwards use the new one, and the Maintain contract
  says so. A crash leaves `locale-<id>.json` under `.aoci/transactions`,
  which the same command resumes while every other command waits; a Root
  whose `#Locale` disagrees with the configured `locale` is the governance
  finding `root_locale_mismatch`, repaired by the same command; an absent
  team file takes the Root's explicit marker as the project Locale.
  `init --locale` on an existing Volumes repository points to this command.
  Ported from dignfei's Locale-switch transaction in #28 (tracked in #34)
  onto the Volumes layout.
- The managed AGENTS block says what to do once cognition is reliable: use
  it as the repository-level system context by default, read only the
  source, tests, configuration, and contracts the task directly needs, and
  widen that evidence only when a specific missing fact could change the
  answer; AOCI never replaces direct source evidence for the objects being
  changed. One sentence in both locales, under "Establishing, generating,
  and restoring cognition"; the rendered `AGENTS.md` and its golden follow.
  Condensed from dignfei's AOCI-first reading wording in #28 (tracked in
  #34); the runtime rules are unchanged.
- `verify`, `check`, and `status` on a Volumes repository tell a person
  what is misaligned and what to do next. `verify` opens with the verdict
  (`Governance: aligned — 6 Entries cover 6 index-role sources`, or the
  result and its finding count), then lists Missing, Stale, Orphan,
  Unbaselined, and review-pending Observe paths one per line, any other
  actionable finding, and a `Next:` line naming the command or Agent action
  that clears it; `check` prints the same lists under its verdict; `status`
  adds one `Governance:` line with the result and the drift counts, computed
  from the same governance facts through the fingerprint cache without
  saving it, and `status --json` carries them under `governance`. Until now
  the Volumes branch of `verify` printed "candidate structure is valid" and
  three hashes before exiting 1, `check` printed a token and a count, and
  `status` said nothing about alignment, so the paths behind a finding were
  reachable only through `--json`. The `init` Scope Proposal line renders its
  largest directories as text (`./ (index 2, observe 0, exclude 0)`) instead
  of Go struct syntax, `scan` says "one Maintain round" when it means one,
  and `docs/getting-started.md` says that `init`'s own files count among the
  index files `scan` reports and which formal assets to commit.
- A declared, enabled database source counts in governance before its
  Database Volume exists. The absent-Volume branch of the shared governance
  facts assessed no sources at all, so a repository could run `database
  source add`, never snapshot it, and stay aligned: verify, check, Maintain,
  and Guide all said so while `database cognition status` alone said
  `snapshot_or_repair_evidence`. Now that source is an `evidence_unavailable`
  finding, the verdict is `evidence_required` with
  `snapshot_or_repair_evidence` as the next action (Maintain stops with the
  snapshot and accept commands), and accepted Evidence with the Volume still
  absent routes to `bootstrap_database_cognition`, which `baseline accept`
  runs itself under `automation.mode=auto`. Bootstrap needs only Code
  governance, so the verdict never blocks the command that clears it; a
  disabled source and an engine without a collector stay informational.
  Found on the SQLite walk-through, which also fixed what a person sees on
  that path: the `unsupported_catalog_feature` error names the operation and
  the table (`operation=catalog_query_sqlite_check, object=t`), `database
  source --help` names SQLite, and the aligned verdict counts Database
  Entries (`6 Code Entries cover 6 index-role sources; 2 Database Entries
  are bound to accepted Evidence`).
- The Legacy-to-Volumes migration walk-through, step by step from
  `docs/upgrading.md`, now reads right for a person. `verify`, `check`, and
  `status` on a Legacy repository say that the layout is read-only since
  0.2.0 and name `aoci cognition onboard start --json`; until now they said
  aligned and ready to commit, and verify's S-coverage note sent the reader
  to `cognition_optimization`, which refuses on that layout (the Legacy
  variant of the note now points past the migration). `cognition onboard
  start` and `next` print the next command under their human output instead
  of a next-action token alone, and `onboard prepare` prints what will be
  written, the terminal command with its phrase, the MCP-dialog route, and
  the apply command instead of the session JSON. The guide itself was wrong
  about one spelling: a completed mapping record's `review_status` and an
  authoring task's `status` are `reviewed` (the template starts them at
  `pending`), not `semantic_reviewed`; a host that followed the guide
  literally stopped at `migration_authoring_task_status_invalid`.
- A Managed Scope change that takes a file out of the Index now says what
  it leaves behind. The walk-through of 2026-11-01 approved "1 files losing
  Index coverage" in the host dialog, `scope apply` said applied, and
  verify, check, and Maintain then stood blocked on the file's Entry, which
  the change had turned into an orphan without a word; retiring cognition
  takes a reviewed candidate set, so the Entry is not removed, but `scope
  apply` (and `activate`, `resume`, `rollback`) now prints the orphaned
  Entries and the `aoci remove-entry --path` or `aoci_remove_entry` step
  that clears them. The approval summary reads "1 file losing Index
  coverage" for one file, the orphan heading verify prints covers a file
  that left the Index role, and `scope rule add`, `update`, `remove`,
  `reset`, and `scope explain` without their argument say which argument
  is missing instead of cobra's "accepts 1 arg(s), received 0".
- A person approves in a terminal by reading what the change does and
  answering `yes`. Every terminal confirmation (`scope approve`, `scope
  safety approve`, `cognition bootstrap approve` and `rollback`, `cognition
  migration approve`, `rollback`, and `reversal approve`) used to demand a
  phrase such as `APPROVE MIGRATION <64-hex digest>` typed exactly, which
  proved nothing the digest-bound approval record does not and was
  incomprehensible to anyone new to a terminal. The prompt now says in plain
  words what approving writes or restores, `yes` in any case approves,
  Enter or anything else rejects with "nothing was changed" and the next
  step, and `--actor` defaults to `human-operator`, so the approve and apply
  commands a paused `scope activate` or `onboard prepare` prints run as
  printed with no `<id>` to replace. The human output puts the host dialog
  first, when the team admits it, and the terminal second. The
  `aoci-host-interaction/v1` contract keeps its shape; `confirmation_phrase`
  is now the word `yes`. Non-TTY callers, piped input, and `--yes` are
  refused as before.
- The final `aoci_update_entry` batch carries its own terminal proof. The
  Apply that brought the last batch to aligned used to prescribe Verify,
  Aggregate Check, and Guide as three more calls whose only purpose was to
  re-derive what that Apply had just computed. It now returns
  `terminal_proof` (`terminal-proof/v1`): the governance result, `aligned`,
  `structure_valid`, `check_passed` (Aggregate Check's verdict),
  `guide_complete` and `guide_next_action` (the Guide's), the composite
  identity, and the actionable findings, computed once from the governance
  fact set all three commands share. The next_action says the cognition
  closing is complete; `next_commands` no longer lists the three commands,
  and `aoci check` stays the CI gate. The shared facts rule over the
  write-side inspector: an Apply whose repository still holds a blocker,
  such as a Database Volume without accepted Evidence, answers
  `aligned=false` with the finding instead of the aligned the inspector
  alone used to claim. The runtime rules, the Maintain tool description, the
  init automation hint, the refresh-ready and observe-review messages, the
  Volumes and refresh specs, and the docs say the same; scenario N1 now pins
  the proof and checks that it agrees with the three CLI commands.
- Orphan Entries are dropped in the update batch. A Code orphan, an Entry
  whose file is gone or left the Index role, used to stop Maintain
  (`explicit_orphan_remove_or_resolve_blocker`) until the Agent removed each
  one with its own `aoci_remove_entry` call and called Maintain again: a
  rename of N files cost N+1 extra calls. Maintain now issues the batch with
  the orphans listed under `orphan_remove_candidates`, and `aoci_update_entry`
  takes an additive `removals` array (each item the path as listed) that
  drops them in the same transaction as the Entries it writes; with nothing
  to author, Maintain answers `remove_orphans_in_update_batch` and one call
  with removals alone closes them. A removal that is not a reported orphan
  is the `repair_required` finding `removal_target_not_orphan` (an unindexed
  path `removal_target_missing`) with zero writes. Verify, Check, and Guide
  report a Code orphan as `authoring_required`; a parallel sibling's applied
  record replays the removal; `aoci_remove_entry` still removes one orphan on
  its own, and a Database orphan still goes through it. Scenario B5 now
  removes the orphan in the batch and refuses a live Entry.
- The Observe review rides with the update batch. When Observe evidence
  (tests, lockfiles, fixtures) moved since the Baseline, Maintain used to
  stop with `review_observed_evidence` until the Agent called
  `intent=observe_review` and then Maintain again: two extra calls on the
  most common iteration, a source change with its test. Under a posture that
  lets the model acknowledge, and when there is a batch to issue, Maintain
  now answers `authoring_required` with the batch and the `observe_review`
  listing, whose `confirm_request` names the batch itself, and
  `aoci_update_entry` takes an additive `observe_review: {review_digest,
  reviewed_by}` that records the review through the same Scope transaction
  before the Entries are written, reported beside the outcome. A digest the
  current list no longer has is the zero-write `repair_required` finding
  `observe_review_stale` with the current listing in
  `observe_review_current`; nothing pending is a no-op. A review posture, a
  listing too long for the transport, a pending Scope Change, and a
  test-only change with nothing to author keep the stop and the
  `intent=observe_review` route, which stays. Scenario N2 now drives the
  batch with the review.
- The real-repository harness reports the two numbers a user waits on:
  `first_build.rounds` and `calls_to_closing`, every MCP call from the first
  Maintain to the Apply whose `terminal_proof` reports aligned, for the first
  build and for the update wave; it drops orphans through `removals` and
  confirms a pending Observe review through the batch, and it stops at that
  Apply instead of calling Maintain once more. On RuoYi (512 Entries) a
  first build is 15 rounds and 30 calls, a 60-file update wave 3 rounds and
  6 calls, with no command to run afterwards.
- Parallel batches are offered as the first-build lever. `aoci scan` says
  what parallel Agent sessions make of its estimate: under the team setting
  `code_cognition_parallel_batches`, the rounds each session takes, measured
  with the cut Maintain makes for that many siblings (`parallel_batches` and
  `parallel_rounds` under `--json`); at the default of one session, what
  four would take and the `config set` that turns it on. A Maintain that
  lists siblings carries one instruction line: hand each to its own Agent
  session, which fetches it by `batch_id`, authors, and applies it, and call
  Maintain again once every sibling is applied. Under a host whose
  subagents share the session's MCP server, a sibling fetched by `batch_id`
  alone carries only the contract's reference, so the line asks each
  subagent for `include_instructions: true`, which returns the complete
  authoring contract with its batch.
- A change to Observe evidence alone closes in two calls. When the
  `observe_review` acknowledgement leaves the repository aligned, its result
  carries the same `terminal_proof` a final Apply does and `next_action`
  `none`, instead of asking for one more Maintain that would only say
  aligned.
- A second `aoci cognition onboard apply` of a completed onboarding answers
  with the result it recorded. It used to record the approval again, set the
  session back to `apply_pending`, and then fail on the recorded
  `apply-result.json` with `onboarding_artifact_conflict`, leaving a completed
  session that claimed an apply was still pending; a session an older binary
  left that way is put back to applied.
- The database acceptance command Maintain returns for `evidence_required`
  runs as printed once filled: it now reads `database baseline accept
  --source {source} --snapshot-sha {snapshot_sha} --json`, where it used to
  lack the required `--snapshot-sha` and was refused. `aoci database
  snapshot` prints the accept command with its digest filled in, the Guide at
  `evidence_required` carries the snapshot and accept commands and names the
  sources that owe Evidence, the status page suggests the snapshot, and the
  `Next:` line of verify and check names `--source` instead of a positional
  argument. A database command without `--source` names the declared
  sources instead of cobra's English `required flag(s) "source" not set`.
- `aoci cognition onboard apply` carries its terminal proof when it leaves the
  repository aligned: it returns `terminal_proof` (the same
  `terminal-proof/v1` the final update batch carries) and no `next_commands`,
  and `onboard status` of a completed session names nothing to run. A session
  that still has governance work names the Guide. Every Legacy repository that
  moves to 0.2 passes this step once. The Legacy migration drill checks the
  proof and cross-checks it against the three CLI readers.
- `aoci init` on a fresh repository says what the first build costs
  before the first scan, the moment a narrower scope is still free: how
  many index files need an Entry, about how many Maintain rounds that takes,
  and what four parallel Agent sessions would make of it; from 20 rounds up
  it prints the exclusion example `scan --dry-run` prints. After the first
  scan, excluding a file that has no Entry yet is a coverage reduction a
  person approves, so the cost is worth reading before roles freeze. A
  one-file estimate reads "1 index file needs an Entry".
- `aoci --help` lists the five everyday commands first (`init`, `scan`,
  `mcp`, `verify`, `check`) under Everyday Commands and the rest under
  Additional Commands, and `aoci scope --help` sorts its seventeen
  subcommands into Policy, Inspect, and Transactions; the group titles are
  locale text assets like every other help string. `docs/getting-started.md`
  is rewritten as the first week in three steps: install and initialize,
  connect the Agent and build the index, keep it aligned.
- A non-Git container root reads each child Git repository through its own
  Git (#54): a directory below the root that holds a `.git` entry is no longer
  walked; its tracked, non-ignored untracked, and ignored paths come from
  `git ls-files` under the same hardened command and boundary checks as a root
  repository, so the child's `.gitignore` holds and a submodule inside it
  stays a boundary. Paths outside any child keep the name-only traversal, the
  container stays a non-Git root, and the Safe Inventory gains the additive
  `child_repositories` and `child_repository_roots` facts. A container indexed
  before this version sees its child-ignored files leave the inventory at the
  next `scan`.
- Incremental Overview delivery (L5) is implemented. `aoci_overview` takes
  `delta_since`, the `scope_identity` of the delivery the Host holds: after a
  passing Attestation and a probe pass over the current identity, the server
  answers `delivery_mode=delta` (or `chunked_delta`) with only the objects
  changed or added since that body, at their current ordinals, the removed
  identities in Metadata, and a Challenge drawn from the delivered objects
  that still echoes the complete identity facts; a passing delta Attestation
  re-anchors the base and a partial or failed one drops it; an unchanged base
  answers an empty delta without a proof. Without a base in the process, an
  unreliable base, a pending `context_compaction`, no probe pass, a delta
  past half the objects, or a delivery the server cannot retain, the call
  answers the complete scope with a named `fallback_reason`. The capability
  manifest lists `overview_delta`; scenario group M (six scenarios) drives it
  through the binary, and two conformance checks pin that `delta_since` is
  refused with `check_only` or a cursor.
- Spec: incremental Overview delivery (L5) was specified in the delivery
  contract first: an ordinary `aoci_overview` carrying
  `delta_since=<scope_identity>`, after a passing Attestation and a probe
  pass over the current identity, delivers only the objects changed, added,
  or removed since that body under the same framing and Chunk rules, is
  attested over exactly that delta, re-anchors on a pass and drops the base
  on a partial or failed Attestation, and answers the complete scope with a
  named `fallback_reason` without a base in the process, without the probe
  pass, during a compaction reload, or past half the objects; the
  conformance checks the implementation must ship are listed.
- Parallel current batches (L4) are implemented. Under the new team key
  `code_cognition_parallel_batches` (absent or 1 is the one-batch flow, byte
  for byte; ceiling 4; `config set` validates it; the capability manifest
  lists `parallel_batches`) one logical plan keeps up to N sibling batches
  outstanding: Maintain delivers the first as the current batch and lists the
  others under `code_plan.siblings`, `aoci_maintain` takes a sibling's
  `batch_id` and delivers it whole, and `aoci_update_entry` accepts the
  siblings in any order. A sibling's Apply is accepted when the plan preimage
  plus the applied siblings, replayed through the editor from the records
  each Apply leaves under `.aoci/drafts/code-cognition`, reproduce the
  current Code Volume; a second Apply arriving under the lock reprojects its
  Entries onto the first's postimage and succeeds. Any other change to the
  Volume, or to the Root, Meta, Database Volume or Scope identity, invalidates
  every outstanding sibling, and one target's source drift invalidates only
  the sibling holding it. `remaining` counts the targets no sibling holds.
  Scenario group L (six scenarios) and two conformance checks pin the
  contract's conformance list.
- The Legacy `baseline scope` refresh is gone: `aoci baseline scope plan`,
  `preview`, `approve`, `apply`, `status`, and `resume`, the
  `internal/scoperefresh` package, and the six `baseline-scope-*/v1` artifact
  versions, which the capability manifest and the release manifest no longer
  list (`baseline_scope_refresh` leaves the planner, apply, and lifecycle
  capabilities; `ordinary_legacy_scope_reduction` leaves the terminal-approval
  lists). Every repository with a Managed Scope Baseline has answered
  `baseline_scope_managed_scope_unsupported` since rc20 and `scope activate`
  establishes Managed Scope for one without it, so no working route is lost.
  A `scope-<id>.json` intent of the retired family left under
  `.aoci/transactions` reads as an invalid scope receipt; move it out.
- The repository's own index has quality floors. `scripts/check-index-quality.sh`
  takes `aoci --json index score` and holds it to
  `scripts/index-quality-floors.txt`: no violation in any of the nine
  dimensions, at most 8 percent of C7+ Entries without an S, a healthy
  Whole-Index budget. CI runs it on every push (`contracts-and-safety`), a
  closure runs it after governance, and the ladder records it as
  `index-quality`. A floor only tightens without a reason in the commit
  message.
- `index score` reads a Cognition Volumes repository. Its nine dimensions
  keep their names and JSON shape; on Volumes they are projected from the
  governance facts `verify` and `check` report, so coverage and freshness
  count the Code drift (a held source is reported, never counted), token is
  the Whole-Index budget, escale is the E scale audit, and Code and Database
  objects are judged under their own Meta dictionaries. The JSON adds
  `layout`, `volumes`, and `budget`; a Legacy score is byte for byte what it
  was. `status --deep` stays Legacy-only.
- A quarterly dependency review joins the run-by-name ladder
  (`dependency-review`, the new `quarterly` cadence, overdue after 92 days).
  `scripts/dependency-review.sh` is a read-only report: the go directive
  against go.dev, every direct Go module against the module proxy, the
  openGauss connector pin against the tags upstream publishes, every GitHub
  Action pin against its newest release and the commit its comment claims,
  and the open dependabot proposals. It upgrades nothing; a bump stays a
  decision taken with its gate.
- A Maintain round issues more candidates on the same transport budget
  (L3; #127 in part). Measured on real trees under the default 24 KiB budget,
  candidates a round before and after: RuoYi 22 to 28 on a process's first
  round and 41 after it, excalidraw 24 to 34 and 47, a 13,850-file tree 20 to
  26 and 39; a first build of RuoYi (512 targets) takes 15 rounds where it
  took 29, excalidraw (798 targets) 19 where it took 34, no round over the
  budget. Four changes to the response and none to what a batch
  binds: a Code candidate no longer repeats `batch_id` (the batch is
  `code_plan.batch_id`, which `aoci_update_entry.code_batch_id` already
  names; Database candidates keep theirs, and a reader of
  `candidates[].batch_id` for Code reads `code_plan.batch_id`); the authoring
  contract (`instructions`, `authoring_meta`) travels once per server process
  and refresh generation and later rounds carry `instructions_ref`, with the
  additive `aoci_maintain` input `include_instructions: true` bringing it
  back and a completed context-compaction reload bringing it back by itself;
  the governance block leaves the four per-asset records off the wire, which
  `cognition_receipt` and `code_plan` already carry; and the budget reserves
  `file_lines` and `expected_e` at the width they will have, taken from the
  fingerprint cache, instead of the widest form. A candidate now binds the
  digest the governance verdict's own snapshot holds instead of reading every
  target again each round. The Guide and the `scan` estimate project the
  first round's shape, so a later round in the same process may issue more
  than the Guide showed.
- Every governance call on a large repository is about three times faster
  (#127 in part; measured by the new `perf-track` contract, 13,850 files: a
  Maintain 3.8 s to 1.3 s, `verify` 3.6 s to 1.1 s, the Guide 3.8 s to 1.5 s;
  1,297 files: a Maintain 0.80 s to 0.59 s, `verify` 0.79 s to 0.42 s). Three causes, none of them the file reads
  everyone assumed: the Managed Scope policy was evaluated over the whole
  tree twice per call, once for the verdict and once more inside the
  business-source manifest, which now takes the state the verdict already
  loaded; glob rules were matched through the regular-expression engine, whose
  backtracking took half of every call on a starter policy (20 rules times
  every path), and are now matched by a token program judged against the
  regexp definition by a differential test over 100,000 pattern-path pairs
  and a fuzz target; and the curation profile re-read every candidate to
  classify it, and now takes the binary verdict and the line count from the
  fingerprint it already had. A stat cache under `.aoci/fingerprints.json`,
  git-ignored and outside every identity, answers an unchanged file by size
  and mtime under git's racily-clean rule; `AOCI_FINGERPRINT_CACHE=off`
  disables it, and the status page and `scan --dry-run` never write it.
- Spec: parallel current batches (L4) are specified in the Cognition Volumes
  contract: a team key
  `code_cognition_parallel_batches` (absent or 1 is today's flow, ceiling 4),
  sibling batches cut from one logical plan against one plan preimage and
  delivered whole by `batch_id`, an Apply preimage rule relaxed exactly to
  "the plan preimage or an applied sibling's postimage" and proven by
  replaying the applied receipts onto the preimage bytes, invalidation of
  every outstanding sibling by any non-sibling change, and the conformance
  checks the implementation must ship.
- Code drift of a Volumes repository is computed in one place,
  `volumegovernance.CodeDrift`, and every reader consumes it: Verify, Check,
  the Guide, Maintain, Overview, the post-Apply inspector that each
  `aoci_update_entry` result reads, and `scope status`. Before, `scope status`
  detected on its own with a trimmed set of walk options and counted held
  sources (empty, binary, oversize, unreadable, curation-excluded) as
  authoring targets, so a tree whose only Entry-less index files were images
  read `authoring_required` there and `aligned` everywhere else. Its `drift`
  now lists them as `skipped` and `curation_excluded`, its `authoring_targets`
  counts what Verify counts, and `drift_warnings` carries the detector's
  warnings. A contract test lists the files allowed to call the detector
  directly, each with its reason (the Legacy readers, the writer that binds
  the active business Baseline), so a new private reader fails the suite;
  two more pin `scope status` and the inspector to the projection on a tree
  with stale, missing, orphan, and held sources.
- Within one server process, a governance call over an unchanged tree no
  longer evaluates the Managed Scope policy or decodes the Baseline and the
  fingerprint cache again: the evaluation is remembered by a digest of every
  input (policy, walk options, curation exclusions, root layout, the walked
  paths), the two documents by the digest of their bytes, so a stale answer
  is impossible and the memo is bounded by the roots a process serves.
  13,850 files: a Maintain 1.09 s on a process's first call, 0.50 s once the
  process has seen the tree; an Overview check 0.27 s. `AOCI_PROCESS_MEMO=off` switches it
  off; `perf_calls.py` now times a third, steady Maintain, since the first
  one creates `.aoci/drafts` and the second therefore sees a new path.
- Black-box: `scripts/blackbox/perf_calls.py` times every governance call a
  user waits on (scan, cold and warm Maintain, Overview check, verify, check,
  Guide, status) against a tree's file count, and `realrepo.py` reports the
  wall time of each tool inside its authoring rounds and of the terminal
  proof; the `perf-track` ladder contract runs the former over five local
  clones from 700 to 13,850 files, so a performance change is read against
  the previous release's numbers rather than claimed.
- Black-box and CI: the conformance suite reports the four receipt-bound
  attestation checks as SKIP, counted but not failing, when the host
  repository is not governance-aligned, instead of four false reds on every
  dirty tree; the scenarios page probe retries a timed-out connection once;
  the PostgreSQL integration job binds a free loopback port instead of 5432;
  `fast-ci` runs on pushes to `v*-line` branches; `full-confidence` splits
  the 55-minute `linux-full` job into `linux-full` (the gate and coverage),
  `linux-blackbox` (suites, upgrade axis, migration drill), `linux-nightly`
  (longrun, fuzz) and `linux-bench`.
- `logs` and `run` are no longer built-in runtime exclusions (#158, the
  second finding). The built-in rule keeps only names that never denote
  source (#100), and both do: `internal/logs` is a package, `cmd/run` a
  command, yet through v0.1.1 every path component of either name was hard
  excluded with no door. Log, PID and socket files stay excluded by suffix,
  `pids` and the PM2 and database runtime names stay built in. New
  repositories exclude a root `logs/` or `run/` through `exclude_root_dirs`,
  which `init` writes; an existing repository keeps its lists and its scope
  identity, and a tracked module of either name becomes a Missing Entry after
  the upgrade, authored like any new source or kept out by adding the name
  to `exclude_dirs` and running `aoci scope activate`. A git-ignored `logs/`
  stays excluded as before.
- SQLite's explicit file source can collect read-only catalog Evidence for
  ordinary rowid tables, columns, primary/foreign keys, and basic indexes
  (Refs #83). Inspect, snapshot, verify, Baseline acceptance, and onboarding
  use the existing Evidence lifecycle, and an enabled SQLite source requires
  Evidence. Unsupported schema features fail closed. No MCP tool or Evidence
  JSON version changes. All hosts using SQLite need this release; 0.1.x
  releases reject the source declaration. The ncruces driver adds three
  release-linked modules without CGO. Read-only WAL collection may update
  SQLite's shared-memory coordination file.

- Built-in sensitive-name rules are a selectable set (#148). `v1` is the rule
  every release through v0.1.1 applied: `.env` and `.env.<name>`, named
  credential files, private keys, `secrets.*`. `v2` adds the shapes
  operational repositories use for credentials: a file name with an `env`
  component after the first (`prod.env`, `manager-login.env`,
  `api.env.local`) and a credential word (`credential`, `secret`,
  `password`, `passwd`, `apikey`, `token`, `api-key`, and their plurals) as a
  whole word of a data or configuration file name (`api-credentials.yaml`,
  `token.txt`, `passwords.json`). Under `v2` a name ending in `.example`,
  `.sample`, `.template`, or `.dist` is a template whatever precedes the
  suffix, a source file such as `tokenizer.go` is never
  matched, and a directory keeps the `v1` classification. The set is the
  team configuration key `sensitive_name_rules`: `init` persists `v2` for a
  new repository; an absent key is `v1` and keeps every existing
  repository's scope identity; `aoci config set sensitive_name_rules v2` on
  an initialized repository is a governed Scope Change whose coverage
  reduction `scope activate` pauses for approval; `aoci doctor` lists the
  indexed paths `v2` would take out. A repository that carries the key needs
  this release on every machine: an older binary evaluates it under `v1`
  and answers `scope_change_required`. The Safe Inventory summary gains
  `sensitive_name_rules`; no MCP tool name, input schema, or formal-asset
  format changes.
- Overview continuation reuses a guarded immutable delivery (#132, whloong).
  The first Volumes request runs the full governance assessment once, frames
  the body, and records a guard over its inputs: configuration, Baseline and
  Curation bytes, the composite CognitionSet identity, Safe Inventory
  membership and Git status, the rules identity and blockers, and every
  index and observe source's raw digest and size. Continuation re-checks the
  guard instead of repeating policy evaluation and rebuilding the body, and
  the proof halves reuse the same delivery. Such cursors start with `v2:`
  and are bound to the MCP Host session: drift answers
  `overview_snapshot_changed`; expiry, eviction, a foreign Host, or a process
  restart answers `overview_session_unavailable_restart_required`, and the
  Host starts again at Chunk 1. Database-enabled repositories, a pending
  scope change, source warnings, and a delivery the server cannot retain
  keep the live path with the reconstructable v1 cursor. The chunk receipt
  stays `overview-chunk-receipt/v1`; Volumes responses gain
  `_meta.aoci_work`; an attestation whose answers use `object` or
  `object_ref` is refused by schema with a message naming `object_identity`;
  the Ledger records the delivery and proof events.
- The Legacy single-file layout is read-only. Its authoring surfaces are
  retired: the `ai` command group and the model endpoint client (the `ai`
  configuration block is still read for compatibility and used by nothing),
  `index build`, `index update`, `index entries`, `index header
  draft|diff|apply`, `index agent plan|stage|header|curation`, `doctor --net`,
  and the Legacy drafting, prompt, workflow, and run-manifest packages. On a
  Legacy repository `aoci_maintain` stops with one finding whose cause starts
  with `legacy_read_only_migrate_required`,
  `next_action=migrate_legacy_repository`, and `next_commands` carrying
  `cognition onboard start --json` and the Guide; `aoci_update_entry`,
  `aoci_remove_entry`, `aoci_report`, `update-entry`, and `remove-entry`
  answer that token and write nothing; `index agent guide` returns a blocked
  guide at that stage, naming any pending transaction receipt and its
  closure; `config set locale` and `init --locale` refuse to change the
  Locale a Legacy index was written in. Reads (`verify`, `check`,
  `status --deep`, `index score`, `index inventory`, `index header show`,
  Overview, search, get_entries, header) and the Legacy-to-Volumes migration
  keep their contracts, and a Managed Scope transaction still retires an
  Entry by disposition or carries the source-bound Entry candidate a stale
  Legacy source needs. A pending `header-*.json` receipt from a Legacy Header
  write is closed with the 0.1.x binary that wrote it; unfinished Legacy
  draft runs are inert. The nine-tool MCP surface, input schemas, and
  formal-asset formats are unchanged; `docs/upgrading.md` has the operator
  notes.
- The engine kernel is importable: `github.com/aoci-spec/aoci-code/engine`.
  `Open` resolves a repository the way the CLI does; `Cognition`,
  `Overview`, `Governance`, and `Identity` project the loader, the delivery
  framer, and the shared governance facts, so a Host's confirmed
  `body_sha256` and the library's digest are one computation; `Connect`
  hosts the nine MCP tools in process over an in-memory transport and
  `ServeStdio` serves them as `aoci mcp` does. `Version` reports the
  build-injected or module version, which now lives in `internal/buildinfo`,
  the ldflags target of every build. `examples/engine-embed` shows the
  embedding, including the openGauss connector replace an importer must
  carry until that connector is published as a module. Contract:
  `spec/public/aoci-engine-library-v1.txt`. No tool, schema, or asset
  format changes.
- A context-compaction reload that cannot fit no longer loops (#114). The MCP
  server watches for a fresh complete delivery started under a pending
  `context_compaction` that is followed by another `context_compaction`
  before it was proven; that interruption is the Host-capacity verdict.
  From then on, in that server session, a fresh request for a scope at least
  that large, made while a compaction refresh is pending, answers
  `delivery_mode=capacity_stop` with
  `fallback_reason=host_context_capacity_exceeded`: no body, the refresh
  generation consumed with an uncertain receipt and the source-bound delivery
  guidance, so the task continues without an unqualified complete-system
  claim. Explicit requests with no compaction pending, smaller scopes, and
  chains the Host already holds still deliver; scoped reads never count; the
  verdict is never persisted. `check_only` gains `delivery_plan` (the whole
  chain's estimated tokens, framed-body bytes, and chunk count) and
  `host_capacity`. Overview Ledger events gain `delivery_chain_id`,
  `chunk_index`, `chunk_count`, `delivery_completed`, `refresh_reasons`, and
  `host_delivery_status`, plus `overview_delivery_interrupted` and
  `overview_capacity_stop` events. The runtime rules, the AGENTS block, the
  Codex post-compaction instruction, and the Overview description state the
  stop; no tool, input schema, or receipt format changes.
- `tools/list` is smaller, a cost every session pays on Hosts that load tool
  schemas up front.
  Descriptions keep what a tool does, when to call it, its write boundary, and
  every contract phrase the tests lock; the procedure they repeated stays in
  `aoci_rules`, the Guide, and the final Chunk's `attestation_prompt`. The
  Overview members `cognition_receipt` and `probe_answers` are listed as plain
  objects while calls are still validated against their closed shapes, so a
  malformed receipt or probe answer is refused exactly as before; the nested
  attestation field descriptions moved to the prompt they duplicated, and the
  single-Entry compatibility fields of `aoci_update_entry` share the `entries`
  item descriptions. The remove-entry description no longer sends a
  non-orphan decision to `aoci_report`, which records nothing since 0.2.0. No
  tool, field, type, or validation rule changes.
- The session contract `aoci_rules` returns is 55% smaller (en-US about
  18.4 KB to 8.3 KB, zh-CN 15.7 KB to 7.7 KB), the other text every session
  reads before its task. Each rule keeps its effect and every phrase and token
  the tests and the manifest lock; what goes is repetition (the ordinal
  definition, the per-reason compaction narrative, the semantic-count
  breakdown, the projection's compatibility notes) whose authority already sits
  in the attestation prompt, the Overview responses, and the specs. The items
  are renumbered 1 to 11. The prescribed success and failure sentences, the
  capacity stop, and every stop condition of a stopped write stay.
- A new production repository starts with thirteen more starter `observe`
  rules, so its first build stops authoring Entries for material that gives no
  system cognition: `third_party/` and `third-party/` trees, `*.svg`, public
  certificates (`*.crt`, `*.cer`; private keys were already a built-in
  sensitive exclusion), and the lockfiles `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`,
  `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`,
  `composer.lock`, and `go.sum`, whose manifests keep the index role. Like the
  first seven, `aoci init` persists them only when no config exists, so an
  existing repository's rules, roles, and scope identity do not change; the
  first seven keep their ids and orders. The lifecycle suite's lockfile
  characterization becomes an assertion that `package-lock.json` is observed
  and never an authoring candidate.
- Migrating a large Legacy index no longer takes hours. Since the Legacy layout
  is read-only, migration to Volumes is how every Legacy repository continues,
  and its mapping template compared each Entry's field atoms by rescanning every
  range, so its cost grew with the cube of the Entry count: one
  prepare-apply-status pass took 47 s at 1,000 Entries, and a 10,000-Entry run
  was still in the template after seven and a half hours. One indexed pass with
  the same attribution rules takes 2.6 s and 28 s; no mapping, receipt, or
  result changes. The nightly benchmark comparison now covers the 10,000-Entry
  migration too.
- A new index no longer publishes the machine it was written on (#76, first
  proposed in #81 by dayebishouji). The first
  directory section of a Code Volume (or Legacy index) recorded the author's
  absolute repository path, often with a user name, and every later section
  continued it into the committed file. A writer creating that first section
  now records the neutral root `/<repository>`; every other section continues
  under it. Readers need no change: no checkout can sit under that root, so it
  resolves the way a clone at another path resolves its author's root, and the
  readers of rc22 through v0.1.1 resolve it and their writers append under it
  the same way. A repository whose path the header grammar could not spell
  back is no longer refused for that reason. An existing index keeps the root
  it records; the format spec and troubleshooting notes say which indexes
  carry which root.
- A person can approve a protected change in the agent's window. Approvals
  used to need a terminal: people did not know they had to open one and type
  a phrase ending in a 64-character digest, and saying no left them with an
  error and no next step. `aoci_maintain` with `intent=human_approval` and
  `approval_request`
  (`kind=scope_change` with the preview a paused `scope activate` saved, or
  `kind=onboarding` for the prepared Bootstrap or Legacy Migration review)
  shows the change through MCP form elicitation, described by AOCI from the
  saved preview or envelope, and records the person's Approve or Reject with
  an optional note for the agent. Approve writes an approval bound exactly as
  a terminal approval is, under the new mechanism
  `host_elicitation_confirmation`, where `scope apply` or `onboard apply`
  reads it, and returns that command; nothing is applied. Reject writes
  nothing and says what to do next. A stale preview is never shown; a host
  without dialogs, a dismissed dialog, and a terminal-only repository get the
  terminal commands. `scope activate`, a non-terminal `scope approve`, and
  `onboard prepare` now carry the call as `host_dialog_request`. The terminal
  prompt says Enter rejects and, on a rejection, what to do next;
  `cognition migration approve` and `cognition bootstrap approve` gain
  `--out-file`. The team key `human_approval_channel` (`tty_or_host_dialog`
  by default, or `tty_only`) decides whether a dialog answer counts, judged
  when Apply starts a transaction and never on Resume; it enters no scope or
  authorization identity. A repository with `safe_inventory_high_risk_opt_in`
  keeps Scope Change approvals in the terminal, and Migration reversal, the
  Migration and Bootstrap rollbacks, and the high-risk pre-read approval stay
  terminal-only. The `aoci_maintain` input schema gains the
  `human_approval` intent and the optional `approval_request` object; the
  capability manifest gains `host_dialog`. An approval recorded in a dialog
  needs this release to apply.

- The Ledger says why a governed call ended where it did (#150). Maintain
  events wrote only `repair_required` or `error`, so waiting for authoring,
  waiting for an observe review, a refused candidate, and a recovery stop
  could not be told apart after the fact, and a failing `check` read as
  `result=ok` beside `exit_code=1`. Ledger schema 9 adds `governance_result`,
  `blocker`, `next_action`, `formal_writes_started`, and `batch_id` to
  Maintain, `update_entries_batch` (and `update_entries_batch_recover`, which
  reconciles Entries already in place), and `human_approval` events, and
  `check_passed` with the verdict to `check` and `verify`, whose `result` now
  only says the command ran. A refused candidate is recorded as
  `repair_required`. The fields are machine tokens; no source, Entry text, or
  connection detail is recorded, and no MCP response changes.
- A Host reviews changed Observe evidence without leaving MCP (#151). A
  Maintain blocked by `observed_pending` carries `observe_review`: each new,
  changed, or removed Observe path with the SHA-256 of its current bytes, a
  `review_digest` binding the complete list, and `confirm_request`, the exact
  `aoci_maintain` call that confirms it. After reading the files the Host
  calls `aoci_maintain` with `intent=observe_review` and
  `observe_review: {review_digest, reviewed_by}`. AOCI recomputes the list;
  when a listed file's bytes moved or the list changed, the call answers
  `status=stale` with the current listing and writes nothing. A current
  confirmation runs the transaction `scope acknowledge` runs, with the same
  Baseline, Ledger, CAS, Recovery, and approval rules, and answers
  `acknowledged` with the confirmed `review_digest`, the count, and
  `acknowledged_paths`; a posture that needs a person saves the preview under
  `.aoci/scope-change/` and answers `human_approval_required` with the dialog
  request and the terminal commands. A list longer than Maintain shows in full
  lists its leading items with `total` and `truncated` and has no MCP
  confirmation, since nothing may be confirmed unseen and the transaction
  acknowledges only the complete set; it keeps the `scope status` and
  `scope acknowledge` route. `scope acknowledge` is unchanged. The
  `aoci_maintain` input schema gains the `observe_review` intent and object;
  no tool is added and no formal-asset format changes.
- A final Volumes Apply whose Entries were already in place no longer calls
  the batch repeated. Resubmitting a stale Entry's identical text is a first
  submission that writes no formal bytes and advances the Baseline, yet
  `aoci update-entry` printed "Repeated batch" and the `aoci_update_entry`
  result's `next_action` named "the repeated final Volumes batch". Both now
  say the Entries were already in place; the `next_action` adds that they
  come from an earlier Apply or an unchanged resubmission and that the
  Baseline binds the current sources. Status, counts, `duplicate_applies`,
  and Ledger events are unchanged.
- The MCP server no longer writes the team configuration. Started on a
  repository whose configuration predates the Locale field, or that has a
  Legacy index and no configuration, it wrote `"locale": "zh-CN"` into
  `.aoci/config.json`, which drifted the bytes a migration envelope or Scope
  Change preview prepared before the server started is bound to, so that
  approval or Apply answered stale. The server now resolves the same `zh-CN`
  without writing it, and an ordinary CLI command still records it. A
  repository that already has its configuration, which `init` writes, sees
  no change.
- A compaction reload that the Host failed to confirm still reaches the
  capacity stop (#154, dayebishouji). A Host delivery confirmation with a
  wrong body hash, a wrong byte count, or no end marker answers
  `host_delivery_incomplete`, and that call also closed the open reload
  attempt, so the compaction that followed restarted the reload at Chunk 1
  instead of answering `capacity_stop`. An incomplete confirmation without a
  model proof half now leaves the attempt open; a model proof half, passing
  or failing, and a complete confirmation close it as before.
- `aoci status` reports an unreadable Baseline instead of a missing one
  (#153, dayebishouji). A corrupt `.aoci/baseline.json`, or a directory in
  its place, read as `baseline_exists=false` with exit 0 and a hint to create
  a Baseline. It now exits 2 with the error envelope under `--json` and a
  message, in the repository's Locale, that names the file, says it was left
  unchanged, and asks for it to be inspected before it is rebuilt. A missing
  Baseline is still a successful status result.
- A SQLite source can be declared (#109, dayebishouji; first slice of #83).
  `aoci database source add --engine sqlite --path data/app.db` saves one
  explicit file, relative to the repository root or absolute, in the `main`
  namespace, with no database name and no credential environment variable;
  URI filenames, `:memory:`, and server-only fields are refused; the
  read-only collector above opens the file. Governance, Database Cognition
  Bootstrap, the policy-bound auto check, Database Entry removal, and
  onboarding collection wait for Evidence only from sources a collector
  exists for, and Verify, Check, and Guide report a source whose engine has
  no collector as the informational `database_source_engine_not_implemented`. The
  team configuration's `database` and `credential_env` fields become
  `omitempty`: a SQLite declaration writes neither, and a server declaration
  is written exactly as before.
- The MCP server runs on go-sdk 1.8.0 (#66). The SDK's newer `2026-07-28`
  revision removes the `initialize` handshake and blocks the server-initiated
  elicitation the host-dialog approval uses, so a client offering it in
  `initialize` is answered with `2025-11-25`. On the wire, `tools/list` adds
  `ttlMs: 0` and `cacheScope: public`, an unknown
  method answers `-32601` instead of code 0, and one inbound frame is bounded
  at 16 MiB. The release binary gains one module, `golang.org/x/time` v0.15.0
  (BSD-3-Clause, from the Go project); `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` lists it.
- The MCP server serves the sessionless `2026-07-28` revision (#66). A client
  on it sends its revision, client information, and capabilities in every
  request's `_meta` and may start with `server/discover`; the `initialize`
  handshake still answers at most `2025-11-25`, and older clients are served
  as before. That revision forbids a server's own requests, so the host-dialog
  approval travels as an input request there: the first
  `aoci_maintain intent=human_approval` call returns the form and a
  `requestState` and writes nothing, and the client calls again with the
  person's answer beside that state. An answer beside any other state is
  `stale` and records nothing, and an accepted form without approve or reject
  is `dismissed`; earlier revisions keep the server's own elicitation request.
  The capability manifest's `mcp_protocol` becomes `2026-07-28` and the new
  `mcp_protocols` lists the five negotiated revisions. The conformance suite
  gains a sessionless lane and the scenarios a sessionless dialog.
- `aoci init` under an existing configuration with no index starts the
  Volume-first layout. It used to write the Legacy minimal skeleton there, for
  example after the aoci files were deleted to start over or under a
  configuration written before `init`, and with the Legacy layout read-only
  the Guide could only route that empty index to a migration. The
  configuration's own settings stay as they were. Only a custom `index_path`,
  which cannot hold a Volumes Root, still gets the Legacy skeleton.
- The Legacy-to-Volumes migration is drilled end to end. `make
  legacy-migration` has the v0.1.0-rc22 release build and align a Legacy
  repository in en-US and one in zh-CN; the binary under test then migrates
  each through onboarding, running only the commands each result names, with
  the approval given in the host dialog, and Verify, Check, and the Guide must
  report the result aligned with every Code Entry carried byte for byte. The
  full-confidence line runs it on every trigger, and `mcp_upgrade.py --fetch
  <tag>` caches one checksum-verified release binary for it.
- A Legacy migration can be followed from its own output. Under `--json` each
  `cognition onboard` result names its continuation in `next_commands`, bound
  to the running binary: the batch command, the receipt command, for a
  Migration the mapping template over the session's own Plan and Snapshot and
  then Preview, then Prepare, and after an Apply that leaves governance work,
  the Guide. A batch with tasks carries `completion_template`, the receipt
  that completes it. A Migration's v1 receipt was refused for carrying the
  `batch_id` that `next` printed; it may now name the batch it completes, and
  a receipt that does not fit is refused as
  `onboarding_completion_contract_mismatch field=<field>`. `cognition
  migration mapping template` gains `--out-file`, which writes the template to
  a new file instead of through a shell redirect that could re-encode it, and
  `docs/upgrading.md` walks through the migration, the candidate and mapping
  files included. Existing fields keep their shape.
- A deletion-only incremental Overview proves itself (#164, dayebishouji).
  A delta that only removes Entries, with Root and Meta unchanged, delivers
  no Entry, so its Challenge has no ordinal; the empty answer list graded as
  zero correct, failed, dropped the retained base, and sent the next
  Overview back to a complete delivery. It now passes on an empty answer
  list with zero reported Entries once delivery is confirmed and governance
  is aligned, and the next delta starts from the new base.
- `database inventory`, `database evidence bundle`, and `database baseline
  accept` refuse a snapshot saved for a replaced source selection (#165,
  dayebishouji). After `database source add --replace` changed what a
  source selects, the old snapshot still answered inventory and the bundle,
  and accept wrote it as the Baseline under the current source ID. The three
  commands now answer `database_snapshot_selection_mismatch` and ask for a
  new snapshot; a refused accept writes no Baseline.
- Update `golang.org/x/sys` to 0.49.0 and the pinned `setup-node` 7.1.0,
  `upload-artifact` 7.0.2, and `goreleaser-action` 7.3.0 Actions (#128,
  #129, #130, #131). The release module set is the same 26 modules and the
  `x/sys` license text is byte-identical. `setup-node` crosses three major
  versions whose breaking changes concern automatic package-manager caching,
  which a repository without a root `package.json` never triggers.
- Update the PostgreSQL driver `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` to 5.12.0 and the
  SQLite collector's `github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3` to 0.36.0 (SQLite
  3.54.1). They move `puddle` to 2.2.3, `go-sqlite3-wasm` to 6.4.35401, and
  `golang.org/x/crypto`, `x/sync`, and `x/text` to 0.58.0, 0.24.0, and
  0.43.0; the pinned `download-artifact` moves to 8.0.2. pgx 5.12.0 fixes
  GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g: from 5.9.0, a server could skip the authentication
  that `require_auth` or `channel_binding=require` demanded, so a PostgreSQL
  source relying on those without `sslmode=verify-full` could be answered by
  an impersonating server. AOCI sends only fixed catalog queries, so the
  exposure was a forged snapshot, not business data. GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq
  does not reach AOCI, which never sends simple-protocol batches. The release
  module set is the same 26 modules, every license text is byte-identical,
  and the license gate binds the SQLite translation's MIT-0 text to
  6.4.35401.


See `docs/install.md` and `docs/supply-chain.md` for asset verification.

name: AOCI-CODE v0.1.1
body:
AOCI-CODE v0.1.1 is built from `a9b803fa47ac2a9c3a2da48209c9030db513612d`.


A security update of the PostgreSQL driver. Nothing else changes: the Go
toolchain, the other dependencies, the MCP tool surface, input schemas,
formal-asset formats, and scope identities are those of v0.1.0, and a
repository aligned under v0.1.0 stays aligned. Upgrade if a PostgreSQL
source's connection string uses `require_auth` or `channel_binding=require`
without `sslmode=verify-full`; MySQL and openGauss sources do not use this
driver.

- Update the PostgreSQL driver `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` to 5.12.0, which
  moves `github.com/jackc/puddle/v2` to 2.2.3. pgx 5.12.0 fixes
  GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g: from 5.9.0, a server could skip the authentication that
  `require_auth` or `channel_binding=require` demanded, so a PostgreSQL source
  relying on those without `sslmode=verify-full` could be answered by an
  impersonating server. AOCI sends only fixed catalog queries, so the exposure
  was a forged snapshot, not business data. GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq does not reach
  AOCI, which never sends simple-protocol batches. The release module set is
  the same 22 modules, and both license texts are byte-identical.
- Known issue, unchanged from v0.1.0: running `aoci cognition onboard apply`
  again on an onboarding that already completed writes the session back to
  `apply_pending`, then answers `onboarding_artifact_conflict`. The formal
  assets and the Baseline are untouched, and Verify, Check, and the Guide
  still report aligned; only the transaction and approval states that
  `cognition onboard status` reads from `.aoci/onboarding/active.json`
  disagree. Run Apply once. The v0.2.0 line returns the recorded result
  instead and repairs a session left this way.


See `docs/install.md` and `docs/supply-chain.md` for asset verification.
